relevant_to: MySQL/Percona all releases and MariaDB (default 200 in both); cannot matter unless statements have IN()/OR equality lists with >= limit values on an indexed column

signals.metric: optimizer trace range_analysis "index_dives_for_eq_ranges" and EXPLAIN ANALYZE estimated vs actual rows for digests with IN lists >= the limit
signals.condition: trace shows index_dives_for_eq_ranges=false and estimated rows differ from actual by >10x with a worse index chosen (skewed data)
signals.why: above the limit the optimizer uses index cardinality averages instead of dives, which on skewed data can pick the wrong index

signals.metric: performance_schema.events_stages_summary_global_by_event_name (stage/sql/statistics, stage/sql/optimizing; needs stage instruments + events_stages_* consumers enabled) share of statement latency for digests with IN lists below the limit
signals.condition: statistics stage is a material share (e.g. >20%) of a cheap statement's latency with hundreds of IN values
signals.why: each equality range costs one or two B-tree dives at plan time; for short-running statements this planning work can exceed execution

impact_bound: bounded by planning time of long-IN digests (statistics-stage time share) when lowering; when raising, by the execution-time difference between the dive-based and statistics-based plan of those digests; typically low (only workloads with long IN lists).

experiment.change: lower to e.g. 10-50 (or raise above the longest IN list) for the session/global
experiment.predict: lowering: statistics-stage time and digest AVG_TIMER_WAIT of long-IN digests fall, plan and SUM_ROWS_EXAMINED unchanged; raising: SUM_ROWS_EXAMINED per call falls because a better index is chosen
experiment.confirm_or_refute: confirm if digest latency moves beyond noise in the predicted direction with the predicted plan; refute if plans are identical and latency unchanged
experiment.cost_or_risk: lowering can cause wrong index choice on skewed data; raising adds planning CPU

collected: partly: digests yes; missing stage summaries for stage/sql/statistics and optimizer trace index_dives_for_eq_ranges for long-IN digests

relevant_to: mariadb only (10.11/11.4/11.8, default 254 buckets); only matters if engine-independent statistics with histograms are collected (ANALYZE TABLE ... signals.metric: mysql.column_stats (hist_size, hist_type, histogram) for columns in WHERE clauses of top digests
signals.condition: histograms absent or 0 for filtered, skewed columns of the expensive digests
signals.why: without a histogram selectivity of non-indexed conditions is guessed, misordering joins

signals.metric: ANALYZE FORMAT=JSON: r_filtered vs filtered per table of top digests
signals.condition: estimated filtered differs from actual r_filtered by a large factor (e.g. >10x) on a column that has a histogram (bucket resolution too coarse)
signals.why: more buckets give finer selectivity estimates for skewed values

impact_bound: at most the time of the digests whose plan is wrong because of the selectivity estimate (requires a better plan to exist); typical low - 254 buckets (JSON_HB in 11.x) is usually enough; gains come from collecting histograms at all rather than size.

experiment.change: raise histogram_size (e.g. to 1024 with JSON_HB in 11.x) and re-run ANALYZE TABLE ... PERSISTENT FOR COLUMNS(...) INDEXES() on the affected tables
experiment.predict: estimated filtered moves closer to r_filtered, join order changes, digest SUM_ROWS_EXAMINED and latency fall
experiment.confirm_or_refute: refute if estimates or plans do not change; benefit is per-statement and must exceed noise
experiment.cost_or_risk: ANALYZE with histograms does a full table scan (I/O, minutes on large tables); larger stats tables
